findings.summary: A repaired landing can also fail while resolving the PR's commits, not only when the head object is missing.
findings.evidence: landing() calls self.commits(&facts.expected_base, &facts.head) before writing. That builds a LandingCommit for each commit, and each one needs a job and a verification record id. A repair after a crash can fail here when the PR's commits or their records cannot be resolved, not only when the head object is missing. Fix: State that WriteFailed also covers a commits() resolution failure. Make sure the criterion 1 fixture has the verification records that commits() needs, so the repair test really writes a record and is not reported as WriteFailed.
findings.location: crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs:1497-1526 (GitLandingRecords::landing) vs plan Risks 'PR head object missing locally'

findings.summary: The plan does not say what 'latest landing record' means.
findings.evidence: The plan never defines 'latest'. It could mean the newest created_at, or the landing whose host_commit sits furthest along main's first-parent line. These two can differ after a repair has written a landing for an older commit. Fix: Define the anchor as the landing whose host_commit appears furthest along main's first-parent walk. Do not use created_at. Cover this in the criterion 5 test.
findings.location: Plan Decision 1 / Step 5 (the 'latest landing record' anchor)

findings.summary: The plan does not say whether reconcile runs before or after land_pr's stop check.
findings.evidence: land_pr runs refuse_if_stopped and takes a per-job lock. The plan says only that reconcile runs 'first', so it is unclear whether reconcile runs before or after the stop check. Fix: Run reconcile after refuse_if_stopped, so a stopped Athena writes nothing, and say so in the plan.

findings.summary: land.rs is listed as a deliverable, but the plan leaves it unchanged.
findings.evidence: Decision 10 says land.rs stays untouched, but it is listed as a deliverable to modify. Fix: Keep the open question in the plan, and note in the producer output that the file was intentionally left unchanged.

summary: I read history.rs, gh.rs (GitLandingRecords::landing, Athena::land_pr, GhClient's ReadPr and default_branch), status.rs and main.rs. The plan matches the request and the accepted reading. The things it names all exist: LandingIntent has head_tree_sha and expected_base, Landing requires an intent, there is a DeclaredIntervention record, HostOperation::ReadPr exists, StatusView has one constructor, and `athena land` goes only through Athena::land_pr. GitLandingRecords::landing already returns the existing record when a landing for the same intent exists, which supports the plan's claim that concurrent runs will not write duplicates. Each demonstration checks the behavior itself: a host call counter, record counts, and output lines from the real status and land paths. Each one would fail if the behavior were missing. The plan honours the bound in criterion 5 and reports the known gap openly. No new athena.toml field is added, and the work fits one producer run. What remains are minor points the producer can handle.
